text:
Ravi (oncall): seeing a sudden attach storm in ap-southeast1 — numerous pods stuck at Attaching and kubelet logs show block-device timeouts :confounded:
Elena (storage): grabbing nvme stats. we're seeing a correlated thermal throttle on a vendor cohort plus an uptick in fsync-heavy replication flushes from cross-region backup jobs at 04:10 UTC
Marco (sre): thermal + sync fsyncs sounds nasty. are these backup jobs new or just rescheduled? we also pushed a driver update last week
Elena (storage): backups were rescheduled to avoid peak but somehow landed exactly when driver GC kicked and the drives hit temp-throttle. pattern: replication workers issue big synchronous writes -> firmware queues slow down async trims -> qdepth collapse -> kubelet attach latency explodes
Ravi (oncall): immediate mitigation suggestions? customers are hitting SLA errors
ops-bot: recommendation: 1) pause low-priority cross-region backups for 15m 2) escalate thermal cohort to vendor 3) enable driver safe-mode (disable aggressive GC) on affected nodes
Marco (sre): also bump local ioQuota on `ap-southeast-gpu` nodepool and cordon the worst-off nodes from new scheduling until temps normalize
Ravi (oncall): pausing backups now via ops UI. running `kubectl cordon node n-ap1-034` on top offenders. patching nodepool ioQuota -> 2x
health-bot: device-temp p95 crossed 78C at 04:10; host-local-io-latency p50 4ms->250ms; attach_pending peaked 29
Elena (storage): short-term we throttled replication workers (async mode) and forced vendor-safe GC delay. attach backlog is trending down after 6m.
Marco (sre): long-term action items: 1) avoid scheduling heavy cross-region flushes during driver-maintenance windows 2) add a replication-aware backoff if device-temp>70C OR attach_pending>8 3) work with vendor to tune firmware async-trim behavior under thermal stress
Ravi (oncall): backlog cleared after cordons + quota bump + pause. keeping 40m monitor. opening ticket INF-2026-THERM-REPL-01 with runbook updates and cost/availability notes (delaying backups increases RPO risk but preserves provisioning SLA)
Elena (storage): adding a runbook snippet: if device-temp p95>75C AND attach_pending>10 -> auto-pause non-critical replication + scale down sync write concurrency
Ravi (oncall): thanks team — will update if it reappears :relieved
